title: Semi-representable objects over a scheme, their coverings and hypercovers
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme with small etale site $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. (1) The category $\mathrm{SR}(X)$ of *semi-representable objects over $X$*: its objects are families $\{U_i\to X\}_{i\in I}$ of objects of $X_{\Et}$ indexed by a set $I$; a morphism $\{U_i\to X\}_{i\in I}\to\{V_j\to X\}_{j\in J}$ is a pair $(\alpha,(f_i)_{i\in I})$ of a map $\alpha:I\to J$ and $X$-morphisms $f_i:U_i\to V_{\alpha(i)}$, composed by composing the index maps and the components. It has finite limits, with final object $\{\mathrm{id}_X\}$ and fibre products as in [lem-weil-pbc-semi-representable-finite-limits] (applied to $\mathcal C=X_{\Et}$). (2) For an object $T$ of $X_{\Et}$, a *$T$-point* of $L=\{L_j\to X\}_{j\in J}$ is a morphism $\{T\}\to L$, i.e. a pair $(j,t)$ with $j\in J$ and $t:T\to L_j$ an $X$-morphism; $L(T)$ denotes the set of $T$-points, and a morphism $L\to L'$ induces $L(T)\to L'(T)$ by composition. (3) A morphism $(\alpha,f_i):\{U_i\}_{i\in I}\to\{V_j\}_{j\in J}$ of $\mathrm{SR}(X)$ is a *covering* if for every $j\in J$ the family $\{f_i:U_i\to V_j\}_{i\in I,\ \alpha(i)=j}$ is a covering family of $X_{\Et}$. (4) A simplicial object $K$ of $\mathrm{SR}(X)$ is a functor $K:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{SR}(X)$, with terms $K_n$, operators $K(\varphi):K_n\to K_m$ for $\varphi:[m]\to[n]$, face maps $d_i$ and degeneracy maps $s_i$ as in [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. Its *matching objects* are: $M_0(K)=\{\mathrm{id}_X\}$; $M_1(K)=K_0\times K_0$, the product in $\mathrm{SR}(X)$ (fibre product over the final object); and for $n\geq2$, $M_n(K)$ is the limit in $\mathrm{SR}(X)$ of the finite diagram consisting of copies $K_{n-1}^{(i)}$ of $K_{n-1}$ for $0\leq i\leq n$, copies $K_{n-2}^{(i,j)}$ of $K_{n-2}$ for $0\leq i<j\leq n$, and the arrows $d_{j-1}:K_{n-1}^{(i)}\to K_{n-2}^{(i,j)}$ and $d_i:K_{n-1}^{(j)}\to K_{n-2}^{(i,j)}$; thus its $T$-points are the tuples $(x_0,\dots,x_n)$ of $T$-points of $K_{n-1}$ with $d_{j-1}x_i=d_ix_j$ for all $0\leq i<j\leq n$. The canonical morphism $K_n\to M_n(K)$ is the one with components $(d_0,\dots,d_n)$ (for $n=0$ the unique morphism to the final object). (5) A *hypercover of $X$ in $\mathrm{SR}(X)$* is a simplicial object $K$ of $\mathrm{SR}(X)$ such that $K_n\to M_n(K)$ is a covering for every $n\geq0$ (for $n=0$: the family $K_0$ is a covering family of $X$ in $X_{\Et}$).
